before:
Tidal Mill Trust — Sluice Attendance Notice

Volunteers on the winter rota are reminded that the sluice is opened on the falling tide only, and that two people must be present at the hatch. Where fewer hands are available than the rota allows, the wheel pit is inspected before the upper race, and the upper race before the visitor walkway. Nothing here takes any of the three inspections out of the round; each is still logged on the board in the mill office before the party leaves. Attendance is written up by the duty keeper, who also notes the tide time and the state of the weed screen. Torches and a whistle are kept in the wooden box beside the lower door.

before:
Long Barn Weaving Guild — Members' Handbook, Section 4: Loom Booking

Looms in the back room are booked in half-day blocks through the diary kept by the door. A block may be extended once on the day if nobody is waiting. Members may leave a warp on a loom overnight when the following block is their own. Bobbins, shuttles and reeds go back into the labelled drawers at the end of every session, and the treadle cords are slackened before the room is locked. Anyone finding a loom out of true should hang the yellow tag on it and tell the workshop steward, who keeps the adjusting tools. The back room is not heated between November and March.
after:
Long Barn Weaving Guild — Members' Handbook, Section 4: Loom Booking

Looms in the back room are booked in half-day blocks through the diary kept by the door. A block may be extended once on the day if nobody is waiting. Members must not leave a warp on a loom overnight, whether or not the following block is their own. Bobbins, shuttles and reeds go back into the labelled drawers at the end of every session, and the treadle cords are slackened before the room is locked. Anyone finding a loom out of true should hang the yellow tag on it and tell the workshop steward, who keeps the adjusting tools. The back room is not heated between November and March.
variation_site: The variation falls in the third sentence of the section.
author_note: Turns a permission into a prohibition with no other content touched.

before:
Marsh End Boatyard Trust — Building Use Policy

The trust holds four buildings on the south quay, and this page states what each is taken to be for the purposes of insurance, keys and the annual return. The lean-to at the north end is held on the register as a store, and the accounts of the last eleven years have been made up on that footing. The tarred shed remains a boathouse, the brick building a meeting room, and the open bay counts as no building at all. Where the standing of a building is altered, the alteration is minuted, the key schedule is reissued, and the insurer is told within fourteen days by letter.

before:
Reservoir Intake — Equipment Setting Sheet

This sheet is filled in at each service visit and kept with the pump house folder. The intake screen sits 1.4 m below summer level and is raked at every visit between April and September. The float switch is set to cut in at the second mark on the staff gauge and to cut out at the fourth. The lag pump follows the lead pump after ninety seconds and the pair alternate weekly. Grease is given to both bearings, four strokes each, and the strainer basket is turned out into the leaf bin. Readings from the hours counter and the flow totaliser are copied into the boxes overleaf before the visit is signed off.

before:
Ferry Slip — Crew Changeover Working

The relief crew join at the slip and the changeover is taken between the eleven-forty and the twelve-ten sailing. The outgoing master hands over the keys, the log tablet and the passenger count, then walks the vehicle deck with the incoming master. The changeover is carried out in Bay 3, with the ramp lifted and the chain across. Nothing may be signed until both masters have seen the deck. If the sailing is running late, the changeover moves to the next full turn round and the office is told by radio. Fuel figures are taken at the same time and written on the sheet clipped inside the wheelhouse door.

before:
Tramway Museum — Volunteer Data Manual, Export Format

The stock list goes to the insurers once a year as a plain text file made by the office machine. Each line carries the four fields separated by commas, in the order fleet number, body type, date of last inspection, and insured value. Dates are given as eight digits with no punctuation. The first line of the file is a heading line and is skipped by the insurer's loader. Lines for vehicles held off site end with the depot letter in brackets. The file is checked by eye against the printed list before it is sent, and a copy is kept in the office cupboard for seven years.

before:
Harbour Office — Winter Bulletin No. 4: Working Hours

For the purposes of everything set out below, a working day begins at 0600 and ends at 1800. The lock is manned throughout each working day and the standby launch is crewed for the first two hours and the last two. The day tariff applies between those hours and the night tariff applies outside them. Notice of an intended movement must reach the office one working day ahead. The three-working-day period for craning bookings is counted the same way. Nothing in this bulletin changes the tariff figures themselves, which are on the sheet issued in October and stand until the spring.
